source_title: Japanese companies compensate users after waves of hacking hit business and economic stability - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Japanese companies are moving to pay financial compensation directly to affected users following a relentless wave of cyberattacks that has paralysed digital services, compromised customer databases and sparked broader concerns regarding national economic stability. According to a report by news agency Reuters, leading the corporate response, GMO Internet Group, a major digital financial and infrastructure services conglomerate, announced that customers will be fully reimbursed for financial losses resulting from unauthorized access following an attack on its foreign exchange trading platform. Additionally, the company will distribute a goodwill payout of 5,000 yen (around $32) to every customer, group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai revealed.Reflecting on the escalating danger facing online operations, Kumagai issued an assessment of the modern digital landscape.âThe internet itself is now starting to break down. The internet is increasingly being transformed into a tool that malicious actors use to threaten and rob people,â wrote Kumagai, whose business footprint spans internet infrastructure, web domains, and cryptocurrency trading platforms.$50 million crypto ransom demanded and rejectedIn an update published on Monday (October 26), Kumagai revealed that the suspected hackers behind the breach issued a financial extortion demand, threatening to publicly leak confidential corporate records and customer data unless the company paid $50 million in cryptocurrency.GMO stated that it will not give in to the extortion demand and is coordinating its incident response closely with law enforcement and regulatory authorities. The company did not draw any link between its breach and the PHP software vulnerabilities that forced public portals offline worldwide last week.Beyond financial payouts, GMO plans to offer a complimentary alternative service to clients for six months. While white-hat security researchers contracted by the firm had previously identified system weaknesses, Kumagai acknowledged that the depth and velocity of internal remediation were insufficient to head off the intrusion.Meanwhile, the mounting corporate fallout has drawn a response from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who confirmed that the administration plans to compile an emergency package of counter-cyberattack measures by next week. As part of a defensive strategy, the government announced that it will establish a specialised unit tasked with simulating AI-driven attacks to expose structural flaws across enterprise and public networks before malicious actors can weaponize them.The initiative follows widespread domestic disruption after critical bugs disclosed in the foundational PHP language triggered millions of automated exploitation attempts globally.Kumagai urged Tokyo to take an aggressive stance under its newly established cyberdefense framework, which took effect this month.
